data.name: Upendar
data.long_meaning: The name Upendar is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Upena' which means 'near' and 'Dharma' which means 'law'. Upendar is a name for a lord or ruler who is near to the law or dharma. This name is often used as a title for deities in Hinduism, indicating their divine status and their role in maintaining the order of the universe.

in_sanskrit.name: उपेन्दर
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: उप (upa) - near, प्रे (pre) - before, इश्वर (ishvar) - lord; Upendar means the one who is present before the supreme lord.

in_hindi.name: उपेन्दर
in_hindi.long_meaning: उप (upa) - near, एक्षा (ekshaa) - desire, वाला (vaala) - possessor, देव (dev) - god; Upendar means the one who possesses the desire to be near the god.

in_tamil.name: உபேந்தர்

It represents a powerful and authoritative figure who is extensively revered for their wisdom, justice, and duty towards maintaining the law and order of the universe. The name is often conferred upon Hindu deities, like Lord Vishnu or Lord Shiva, as a title signifying their ultimate power and their role as the upholders of dharma, the universal law.

historical_references.context: Upendra was a powerful and just ruler who is remembered for his charitable acts and his efforts to spread the teachings of Jainism in his kingdom. He is mentioned in various Jain texts and is considered a revered figure in Jain history.

historical_references.reference: Another Upendra is mentioned in Hindu mythology as the lord of the northern direction and the presiding deity of north India.
historical_references.context: Upendra is also known as Indra, the god of rain and thunder, and is often depicted riding on an elephant named Airavata. He is one of the primary gods in the Hindu pantheon and is invoked during various religious rituals and festivals.
